Today Apple celebrates the opening of its Advanced Manufacturing Center located in Houston, Texas. Details below.

Apple Will Train Business Leaders at Its Newly Established Houston Advanced Manufacturing Center

Apple today opened its new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center offers free training and educational courses to small and medium-sized businesses, allowing them to gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge equipment, interactive labs and a variety of tools to accelerate innovation. The AMC is located within the same Houston facility responsible for manufacturing and shipping Apple's advanced AI servers, and will begin producing Mac mini this year. […] Apple CEO Tim Cook said: "In just nine months, we have invested hundreds of millions of dollars in this Houston facility. We built the factory, commenced production, and shipped our first advanced AI servers out the door. Today, we are excited to open our new Advanced Manufacturing Center, a place where businesses, workers and students can learn the same innovative processes we use to manufacture Apple's most breakthrough products. We also look forward to kicking off Mac mini production later this year. We believe in American workers and American creativity, and we are moving forward at an incredible pace — because we don't just want to create outstanding products, we want to build the future of American manufacturing."

Tim Cook announced via his social media that he made a special trip to Houston to attend the opening ceremony. The launch event will be attended by several government officials, including U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Representative Christian Menefee, Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis, and others.

The AMC spans 20,000 square feet, where Apple experts will "directly share their knowledge with participating businesses and entrepreneurs to help accelerate the development of smart manufacturing in America."

The first group of business leaders arrived today to take part in the inaugural training session. The day's curriculum focused on smart manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
